POSITION: 'near the hilt' is contradicted by what I see — the foliage sits mid-to-upper blade with a clear bare gap above the crossguard. ATTACHMENT: 'growing along' asserts the sprig is attached, and both reviewers independently said this is undeterminable (reviewer-a: 'whether the green sprigs near the blade are attached to the sword or are background foliage passing in front of it cannot be determined'; reviewer-c: 'whether the foliage on the blade is growing from it or merely draped over it is not determinable'), as did the generating model's own self-reported uncertainty. I did NOT take AUTO_CORRECT: only reviewer-c raised the position error, reviewer-a passed and never stated a position along the blade, so gate 2 (two independent reviewers reporting the same thing) is not met, and the schema says to step away from AUTO_CORRECT when hesitating. Dropping this single item is the lowest-loss move: the sword itself, the bird, the vines, the path, the mushrooms and the flowers are all independently confirmed by both reviewers and stay intact.

independentFinding: I counted the image myself before opening the packet. Engraving-style card: one prone figure lying face-down on barren stony ground, head to the left, legs to the right, both arms flung outward with open empty hands, rust-red cloak bunched over the back, blue-grey tunic and pale wrist cuffs. Blades stand upright out of the back, driven point-down. I enumerated the round pommels one at a time against the open sky, left to right: (1) far left, low; (2) left, tall; (3) left-of-centre, medium; (4) centre-left, the tallest; (5) centre, the short low one; (6) centre, tall; (7) centre-right, medium; (8) right, medium-tall; (9) far right, low. NINE pommels. The pommels are silhouetted separately against sky and do not overlap each other — only the blade shafts overlap further down where they converge into the body. No tenth pommel breaks the skyline anywhere in the fan. Background: dark hatched storm sky, a low sun on the sea horizon at right with a light column on the water, a dark flat-topped cliff at the far left horizon.
reason: All five gates are met. (1) The count is unambiguous on the specific thing being asserted: the existing text claims 'ten upright swords with round pommels and straight crossguards', and pommels are exactly what IS individually resolvable here — both reviewers note the pommels do not overlap, only the blades do. There are nine. (2) TWO independent reviewers reported it: reviewer-b and reviewer-d both counted nine, both verdict 'corrected'. (3) I reached nine independently, before reading either. Decisively, all three enumerations match slot-for-slot by position and height — far-left low, left tall, left-of-centre medium, centre-left tallest, centre short, centre tall, centre-right medium, right medium-tall, far-right low. Three blind passes agreeing on nine LOCATIONS, not merely on the number nine, is what lifts this past the reviewers' individually hedged 'medium'. (4) Count is an observable fact. (5) Three exact substring replacements, each verified present and unique in the reveal packet with grep -F. On the reviewers' shared caveat that a fully occluded tenth blade cannot be ruled out: that residual applies to any count and cannot be evidence FOR ten; meanwhile 'ten' is the number the card-name prior would supply, which is precisely the failure mode this round exists to catch, and reviewer-d explicitly recorded refusing to adjust toward an expected total. I kept the word 'upright' in the scene string: the blades are driven point-down into the back but stand upright, so 'upright' is accurate and only the numeral needed changing. I also patched the model's own self-reported uncertainty line so the file does not keep asserting ten after the correction.
